candidates.name: Congenital hydrocephalus
support_spans: bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns
candidates.why: The presence of bilateral ventriculomegaly is a key feature of congenital hydrocephalus.

candidates.name: Fetal ventriculitis
support_spans: irregular ventricular walls
multiple hyperechoic regions with indistinct margins within the ventricular lumens
candidates.why: The irregular ventricular walls and hyperechoic regions within the ventricles are suggestive of fetal ventriculitis.

candidates.name: Cytomegalovirus infection
support_spans: multiple hyperechoic regions with indistinct margins within the ventricular lumens
contradict_spans: A comprehensive workup—including a TORCH panel... returned within normal limits
candidates.why: Cytomegalovirus infection can cause fetal ventriculitis and hydrocephalus, but the normal TORCH panel results contradict this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Toxoplasmosis
support_spans: bilateral ventriculomegaly
contradict_spans: A comprehensive workup—including a TORCH panel... returned within normal limits
candidates.why: Toxoplasmosis can cause congenital hydrocephalus, but the normal TORCH panel results contradict this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Dandy-Walker malformation
support_spans: bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns
candidates.why: Fetal MRI can confirm the diagnosis of Dandy-Walker malformation, which is characterized by bilateral ventriculomegaly and hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis.

candidates.name: Aicardi syndrome
support_spans: bilateral ventriculomegaly
irregular ventricular walls
candidates.why: Fetal MRI and ultrasound can suggest the diagnosis of Aicardi syndrome, which is characterized by bilateral ventriculomegaly, irregular ventricular walls, and other CNS anomalies.
